title: The legacy key is withdrawn while the Work Package still asks for an APP story under the legacy title
source: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 rows Status, Decision, Withdrawn IDs and Later home; _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md story line RWB-P1-DM001-APP; Template and Rules v1 §R5.2 and §R6
section: 1 Story; 2 Business rationale; 7 Acceptance criteria; 19 Out of scope
description: D-RCV-35 (U1) removed the legacy story: Status Removed, Decision D-RCV-35 (U1), Withdrawn IDs 'AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04'. The Work Package still lists an APP story under the legacy title 'Migrate account and arrears', with no legacy AC to copy and no legacy test text to carry, and it says nothing about what the story then delivers. Read as written, the slice would have no deliverable; read as a migration, it would contradict the decision that removed the migration.
evidence: Data Migration Stories v3 line 15 'Removed by D-RCV-35. The data is already in ACE.' with the Status, Decision and Withdrawn IDs rows; WP B-P1-06 story line with acs [] and tcs_legacy ['TC-DM-001-01','TC-DM-001-04']
proposed: Keep one APP story per the Work Package and read it as the rework that replaces the migration: the account and arrears read path over the four views and the per-service Flyway version that creates nothing for those rows and records the removal. Keep the legacy title because §R5.2 keeps the legacy compact and title, and correct the title in the next story-master version so that it names the read path, with the story key and the legacy key unchanged.

title: The account and arrears read path is given as a legacy row, not as a deliverable with an answer shape or a cut-off
source: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 row 'Read path instead'; FSD P1 v3 A2.3 'What this module does instead' and A2.14; TSD P1 v3 T3.3, T3.4 and T3.7; Template and Rules v1 §R7.3
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 8 Business rules; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: The sources name the four views and the DP01 row, and they name the account read as a path rather than as a story: no source gives the answer shape, the paging, the field order, the not-found behaviour, or the per-source cut-off that marks DP01 late. The freshness rules give the status vocabulary and the message but not the cut-off value, and this story's pattern set holds neither DP-06 nor DP-07, so no parameter or reference read is available to it.
evidence: Legacy row 'Read path instead' names the views only; TSD P1 v3 T3.7 gives 'the source cut-off (configuration, per source)' with no value; FSD P1 v3 A2.14 gates on a complete ACE batch without a cut-off value
proposed: Fix the read as the four views keyed by account_key at the ACE business date, with the answer shaped by the P1 read contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and the field order taken from the field IDs, and with the late case answered from v_ace_batch_status and MSG-P1-001 with no parameter read. Revisit only when a per-source cut-off is agreed as a rwb-case parameter.

title: A Day-1 story is tagged wave 4 while its service is wave 1 and the account read is needed by the wave 1 case screens
source: _work/msr/wp/B-P1-06.md story line (wave 4, business_epic EP08, ready Day 1, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON); Template and Rules v1 §R5.6 and §R5.7; Architecture v5 service table (rwb-source-data wave 1)
section: 3 Preconditions; 9 State transitions; 18 Traceability
description: The Work Package fixes wave 4 and business epic EP08 for this story, and Day 1 readiness on one platform contract. §R5.6 keeps the W-MAP wave only where the business epic is earlier than the service wave; here the W-MAP wave (4) is later than the service wave (1), so the story is tagged wave 4 although its read path is the account source of the wave 1 case screens. The build is not blocked, but the release tag and the date of the read path are not settled by any source.
evidence: WP line: wave 4, business_epic EP08, ready 'Day 1', H ['RWB-PLT-E1044-CON']; §R5.6 wave map EP08 to 4; Architecture v5 service table puts rwb-source-data in wave 1; FSD P1 v3 A2.18 case list reads v_ace_account
proposed: Build from Day 1 as fixed, and release the read path with the wave 1 service deploy, where the P1 read contract and the freshness stamp are live; keep the wave 4 tag as the tag of business epic EP08 and confirm the release date at the wave entry check.

title: The account operation named by the architecture is absent from the TSD P1 endpoint inventory, and the answer field names are in no module specification
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 P1 IN and slide 29 (login rwb_source_data); TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 §R3 precedence
section: 3 Preconditions; 12.1 REST operations provided; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.9 Call-type summary; 13 Solution plan

TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A lists API-P1-001 to API-P1-016 and holds no account operation, and neither document gives the answer field names of the account read. The service base /api/recovery/source-data/v1 follows from §R4 and DP-13, so the base is not in doubt, but the operation, its parameters and its answer are.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 lines 1075 and 1114 (P1 IN: REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}) and line 2063 (login rwb_source_data); TSD P1 v3 Appendix T-A.1 endpoint inventory; §R4 and DP-13 for the base
proposed: Take the architecture under §R3 (rank 1 over rank 6): the read is answered behind GET /accounts/{id} on /api/recovery/source-data/v1, one hop, 2 s, published by RWB-P1-E1069-APP, and this story adds no path of its own. Add the operation and its answer schema to the next TSD P1 version and to RWB-P1-E1069-CON.

title: The withdrawn migration's file name and its test text are held by no source
source: Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3, RWB-DM-001 row Withdrawn IDs; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.10; Recovery Workbench Test Cases master
section: 13 Solution plan; 16 Test cases
description: The legacy key withdrew TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04 and named no migration file, and the withdrawn test text is not in the masters that this run reads. The story therefore cannot assert the absence of a named migration file and cannot copy the withdrawn text: it asserts that no version of the sequence names an extract, a transform, a load or a reconciliation of migrated account or arrears rows, and it keeps the two legacy test case IDs with new Covers.
evidence: Legacy row Withdrawn IDs 'AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-001-01 to TC-DM-001-04'; no migration file name in the legacy section or in TSD P1 v3 T3.2 and T3.10; WP tcs_legacy ['TC-DM-001-01','TC-DM-001-04']
proposed: Keep the two legacy test case IDs with the new Covers and record the full new test in the test case master under the same IDs; do not invent a migration file name, and close this row when the master's next version records the withdrawal.

title: The legacy key is Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1) while the Work Package still asks for an APP story under it, so the story states a withdrawal and a build in one document
source: Legacy RWB-DM-002 rows Status, Decision, Why, Read path instead, Data product and Withdrawn IDs (04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md, file header lines 1-11 and the RWB-DM-002 section); Work Package B-P1-06 story line RWB-P1-DM002-APP; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 change note for version 3 and A2.2; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.10; Template and Rules v1 R-PREC (source precedence) and R6
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 7 Acceptance criteria (closing note); section 9 State transitions; section 19 Out of scope
description: Two levels of the same key disagree. The legacy story master (precedence level 9) marks RWB-DM-002 Removed by D-RCV-35 (U1) and withdraws AC1 to AC3 and TC-DM-002-01 to TC-DM-002-04, because ACE ingests the SCBPDM customer, phone, e-mail and address data and holds the one copy. The FSD and TSD P1 v3 (precedence levels 7 and 6) are re-based on the same decision and remove the tables party and contact_point. The higher sources therefore win and the migration cannot be built. The Work Package B-P1-06 nevertheless lists RWB-P1-DM002-APP as an APP story to be written for this legacy key with two retained test case IDs and no legacy AC. The result is a story that must both record a withdrawal and deliver a build: the read path that replaces the migration. No source states that the replacement read path is the intent of the legacy key, and no source names the story that would own it if this one were retired instead.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-002 reads 'Status | Removed', 'Decision | D-RCV-35 (U1)', 'Withdrawn IDs | AC1 to AC3; TC-DM-002-01 to TC-DM-002-04'; the legacy file header reads 'Two stories leave because the data is already in ACE (RWB-DM-001, RWB-DM-002)'; the Work Package line reads "id": "RWB-P1-DM002-APP", "wt": "APP", "disposition": "Split (rework)", "acs": [], "tcs_legacy": ["TC-DM-002-01", "TC-DM-002-04"]; TSD P1 v3 T3.10 reads 'party | 13 | Copy of SCBPDM data (U1) | v_ace_customer; flags to party_ext' and 'contact_point | 8 | Copy of SCBPDM data (U1) | v_ace_contact; consent and quality to contact_point_ext'.
proposed: Keep the withdrawal and keep the story: confirm in the Change Register and the story catalog that RWB-P1-DM002-APP is the rework of the withdrawn key and delivers the read path only, that no extract, load, reconciliation or cutover is in its scope, and that its two retained test case IDs carry new text. If the programme prefers retirement, the read path must be moved to a named story of P1 before this one is closed, so that DP02 has an owner.

title: The read path that replaces the migration is described in one legacy row only: no source fixes the fields the answer carries, the join of a person to many contact points, or the use of the two extension tables beyond their column list
source: Legacy RWB-DM-002 row Read path instead; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1.3.2 field catalog and A2.2 DP02 row; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.3 (v_ace_customer, v_ace_contact, v_ace_ca_relation), T3.5 (party_ext, contact_point_ext) and T3.9 (business-key links); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 37 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R7.3 (fill order) and R9
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 4 to 7; section 7 AC2 and AC4; section 11 Data; section 13 Database and migrations and Configuration and reference data
description: The replacement of the migration is given as one prose row ('v_ace_customer for the customer and the masked identity, v_ace_contact for phone, email and address, v_ace_ca_relation for the borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles, and party_ext and contact_point_ext for the Workbench flags and consent'). It does not say which of the 20 customer fields, 9 contact fields and 5 relation fields an answer returns, whether an answer returns one row per contact_key or one row per person, which of the extension columns are read on the customer read path as opposed to a later screen, or how a person with no extension row is answered. The TSD gives the columns and the 1:1 cardinality (T3.5, T3.9) but no read-path shape, and the FSD field catalog lists the extension columns without saying which of them the customer read returns.
evidence: Legacy RWB-DM-002 'Read path instead | v_ace_customer for the customer and the masked identity, v_ace_contact for phone, email and address, v_ace_ca_relation for the borrower, guarantor and co-borrower roles, and party_ext and contact_point_ext for the Workbench flags and consent'; TSD P1 v3 T3.9 reads 'party_ext | person_key | v_ace_customer.person_key | 0 or 1 to 1' and 'contact_point_ext | contact_key | v_ace_contact.contact_key | 0 or 1 to 1'; TSD P1 v3 T3.5 gives the 12 and 14 columns with no read shape; FSD P1 A2.1.3.2 gives the flags and consent columns with no consumer named.
area: rwb-source-data customer and party read path
proposed: Fix the read-path answer in the contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP (the operation that serves it) as: the customer fields of v_ace_customer, one row per contact_key of v_ace_contact, one row per account of v_ace_ca_relation, the four party_ext flags as an optional object, and the consent and quality of each contact row; state that a person with no extension row is answered with the object absent and not with defaults. Keep the field names in the physical schema and the dictionary, not in code.

title: Where the masking of the ACE-sourced personal fields is answered is fixed in another service's story, while this story may declare no contract dependency and no masking pattern
source: Legacy RWB-DM-002 rows Read path instead and Why; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1.3.1 (BR-P1-001-6) and the A2.15 identity-masking text; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T3.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 12, 14 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-08 and DP-11; Work Package B-P1-06 story line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP (C empty, patterns DP05 and DP15)
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow step 8; section 7 AC3 and AC6; section 8 BR3; section 10 Authority; section 13 Build steps
description: The masking of the ACE-sourced personal fields is decided in rwb-access (P4): the policy and masking rows are P4 data, the authorise contract answers masked or clear per field ID, and Architecture v5 says masking is applied by rwb-source-data. The Work Package fixes this story's contract dependencies as empty and its patterns as DP05 and DP15, so the story cannot declare the rwb-access authorise contract as a C dependency (DP-08) even though that is where the answer comes from. No source states which consumer applies the masked rendering of v_ace_contact.contact_value for the case screen, nor whether the answer of this service carries a masked rendering or only the raw value plus a marker.
evidence: FSD P1 v3 A2.15 reads 'Phone, email and address come in full from v_ace_contact, because notices and calls need them, and are masked at the API by role'; FSD P1 v3 BR-P1-001-6 reads 'A view never exposes customer.identification_number in clear; it returns id_no_masked and id_no_last4 only'; TSD P1 v3 T3.4 reads 'The identity number is never exposed in clear'; Architecture v5 slide 12 reads 'masking is applied by rwb-source-data'; RWB-P4-E1069-APP writes the masking rows and answers masking on POST /authorise; the Work Package line reads '"patterns": ["DP05", "DP15"], "C": []'.
proposed: Record in the Service Contract Catalog that the masking answer for an ACE-sourced field is taken by rwb-source-data on the rwb-access authorise decision, and add the contract dependency to the story or to the platform guard library at the next revision of the plan; until then the story applies the answer as the service standard and keeps the dependency row as the Work Package fixes it.

title: A wave 4 story is marked Ready to start Day 1 on a platform Flyway contract, and the readiness rule does not name the case
source: Work Package B-P1-06 story line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP (wave 4, ready Day 1, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON); Template and Rules v1 R5.6 (W-MAP), R5.7 rules 2, 3 and 8; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 6 INVEST check; section 13 Feature switch
description: The story sits in wave 4 by the W-MAP of business epic EP08, and its only build dependency is RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, a platform contract story of wave 0. Under R5.7 rule 8 a story ready on CON dependencies only is Day 1, so the metadata is internally consistent; what is not stated is whether a wave 4 story may start on Day 1, or whether Day 1 readiness is a statement about the dependency graph only. The service itself is wave 1 in the service table, which makes the wave 4 tag a business-epic tag and not a delivery wave. No source resolves the two readings.
evidence: Template and Rules R5.6 maps EP08 to wave 4 and R5.7 rule 8 reads 'Ready to start = "Day 1" if the story has only CON H dependencies'; the service table gives rwb-source-data wave 1; the Work Package line reads '"wave": 4, "ready": "Day 1", "H": ["RWB-PLT-E1044-CON"]'.
proposed: State in the Day-1 Work Allocation that Ready to start is computed from the dependency graph only, so a story whose business epic is wave 4 may be picked up on Day 1 when its build edges are platform contracts; and keep the wave tag as the business epic tag it is.

title: The read operation, its request and answer field names, and the feature switch of the read path are owned elsewhere or named by no source, while the story must still build and be switched
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 15 and 41; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.14 and A2.15; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T-A (endpoint inventory, absence of the customer read path); Work Package B-P1-06 story line for RWB-P1-DM002-APP; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-11 and the R-PREC default ruling on feature flags
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 and AC2; section 12.1 REST operations provided; section 12.8 Contract fakes; section 13 Configuration and reference data and Feature switch
description: Three values the story needs are not in any source it may read. (1) The read of a customer and its parties is the operation GET /customers/{id} of rwb-source-data, which the Work Package assigns to RWB-P1-E1069-APP; this story therefore claims no path, no parameter and no response schema, but it still needs the answer field names to build the repository behind it, and the TSD endpoint inventory carries none of them. (2) The two preconditions of the read path (RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-DB) are not build edges in the Work Package, so the story must be buildable from contract fakes on Day 1 and the plan records no edge. (3) The feature switch of the read path is a parameter of the platform flag library by the R-PREC default ruling, whose key, default and off behaviour no source names.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 (P1 contract) reads 'REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id}; GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId=; GET /freshness (business date); POST /business-days/{date}/ready (Airflow)'; the Work Package line reads '"H": ["RWB-PLT-E1044-CON"], "C": [], "X": []'; Template and Rules R3 default rulings give feature flags to the platform library; no extract names a flag key or an off behaviour.
proposed: Publish the customer and party answer schema in the RWB-P1-E1069-APP contract with its field names and its not-found and stale shapes; record RWB-P1-E1069-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-DB as preconditions of this story in the Dependency Map without adding an H edge; and fix the read-path switch key and its off behaviour in the Service Template Specification.

title: RWB-P1-E1001-APP: schema-split mechanics, login name, extension-table delivery boundary and Arch v5 against FSD and TSD P1
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 15, 29, 41 and 45; TSD P1 v3 T3.1 to T3.6; FSD P1 v3 A2.1 and A2.2; Ownership Map part tables; Template and Rules v1 R6
section: Sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 12 and 13
description: Four points are open for this story. (1) The built migration V0001__rwb_e1_001_recovery_schema.sql in schema recovery is kept as built and is not rewritten, so P1's 18 tables need a new per-service Flyway file on rwb-source-data's own sequence; which sequence number, and whether the split migration or a separate DB story creates P1's own tables, is not stated, and the split plan holds no RWB-P1-E1001-DB story. (2) Schema and login are named rwb_source_data on slide 29 and slide 41, but no source states the rule for a login whose service short name contains a hyphen. (3) The four extension tables are P1's data and are delivered by RWB-P1-E1069-DB, while their 49 dictionary fields must exist before the tables do, so the conformance test cannot report 1,062 of 1,062 fields until RWB-P1-E1069-DB has run. (4) Arch v5 slide 15 gives P1 the REST contract of /customers, /accounts, /collateral, /payments, /freshness and /business-days/{date}/ready, while FSD P1 v3, TSD P1 v3 and the API Specification also give P1 the data product, dictionary and data contract operations, and Arch v5 slide 41 lists P1 as owning the ACE view contract, the extension tables, freshness and reconciliation only, not the catalog and the dictionary tables.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 rwb-source-data IN and OUT lines; slide 29 schema and login panel; slide 41 P1 row; slide 45 'Who reads ACE data'; TSD P1 v3 T3.2 two-migration rule and T3.5 extension tables; FSD P1 v3 A2.1 and A2.2; Ownership Map part tables (data_product, sys_objects, sys_fields, data_contract owned by P1); split_plan.json holds no RWB-P1-E1001-DB
proposed: Adopt the five assumptions below for wave 1: keep the built baseline as built; create P1's 13 own tables in rwb_source_data from this story's split migration; name schema and login rwb_source_data; leave the four extension tables to RWB-P1-E1069-DB while this story seeds their 49 dictionary fields; keep the catalog, the dictionary tables and the v_data_dictionary read model in rwb_source_data with no REST operation added by this story; and confirm in the verification loop that the catalog, dictionary and data-contract operations of the P1 contract stay with RWB-P1-E1064-APP, RWB-P1-E1015-APP and RWB-P1-E1016-APP

title: DP-17 removes the INT-19 lake extract and the Power BI feed that legacy AC3 and AC7 assert
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 37 and 41 and the DP table of Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 (DP-17); Interface Specifications v3 (INT-19 and INT-20 removed); legacy RWB-E1-013 AC3 and AC7
section: RWB-E1-013 §7 Acceptance criteria, §12 Contract and §13 Solution plan; FSD P1 A2.12 and A2.19
description: Legacy AC3 asserts an INT-19 extract in the data lake for the business date with a freshness stamp and a record count in its trailer, the baseline rows of 2026-11-27 unchanged inside it, and a JOB-15 run in the job monitor. Legacy AC7 asserts the extract held when the lake does not answer, an alert to the operations channel with MSG-GEN-006 naming the lake, and the resend in the next window. DP-17 removes the data lake, INT-19 and INT-20 and connects no Recovery service to a lake or to Power BI, so neither criterion has any P1 deliverable; no source restates them on a target path in rwb-source-data, and the publish and the hold survive only on the P9 publication.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 8 note (no connection to the data lake; INT-19/INT-20 are removed), slide 37 (INT-19/20 removed), slide 41 P1 DB line (schema rwb_source_data holds no lake object) and slide 44 (JOB-15 is an Airflow trigger with no data lake); TSD P1 v3 T5.1 still lists INT-19 as an outbound interface
proposed: Read AC3 and AC7 as superseded by DP-17: the publish, the hold and the alert move to the P9 publication and its ReportPublished event, rwb-source-data supplies the gate and the freshness the publication reads, and the lake extract, the trailer, the Power BI data set and the resend are recorded as removed with no replacement in wave 1.

title: The P1 functional and technical specifications still describe the lake publish that DP-17 removes
source: FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.12.2 and A2.13.2; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T5.1 (INT-19 outbound) and T3.6 (lake_copy_watermark)
section: FSD P1 A2.12 Integration points and A2.13 step 2; TSD P1 T5.1 row INT-19 and T3.6
description: The FSD P1 module names Power BI and the data lake as integration points of the daily reconciliation and freshness report and states that a held case list keeps the lake on the previous released date, and the TSD P1 module keeps INT-19 as an outbound interface and the table lake_copy_watermark. Arch v5 removes the lake, INT-19 and INT-20, and the ownership map has no target for lake_copy_watermark, so the two specifications describe a destination this service no longer has.
evidence: Arch v5 slides 8, 37 and 44 and the removal note on Interface Specifications v3; ownership map ruling on lake_copy_watermark (no target, P1 drops it); DP-17
proposed: Mark the lake steps, the INT-19 row and lake_copy_watermark removed in the next FSD and TSD versions of P1, and keep the publish status of the case list and the reconciliation result, which carry no lake dependency in the target.

title: RWB-E1-013 is split across four stories and no single source assigns each legacy acceptance criterion
source: RWB-E1-013 (one P9 module, eight acceptance criteria); Template and Rules v1 §R6 and §R5.2; Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41

title: The 05:30 late check and the worker and queue registration have no story in the build dependencies of this slice
source: Architecture v5 slides 31, 32 and 44 and TSD P1 v3 T3.7; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 (DP-10) and §R5.7
section: RWB-E1-013 §12 Contract (job JOB-15); this story §12.6

The DP table gives DP-10 the dependency H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (the workflow kit contract), but the story that registers this service's Schedule, workers and queue is named by no source, and this Work Package fixes the build dependencies of this secondary slice as None. The registration therefore stands outside the build dependencies of this story.

owner_role: DevOps team and platform workflow owner
proposed: Let the platform workflow and operations stories of the epic register the 05:30 Schedule, the rwb-source-data worker, the task queue and the topic with its retry and .dlt topics, and record the dependency as a note of section 12.6 and an external or operations dependency in the plan rather than as a build dependency of this slice.

title: No measure value, definition or snapshot is produced or read by the P1 slice of RWB-E1-013
source: Ownership map (measure_definition and measure_snapshot owned by P9); TSD P1 v3 A2.19 and TSD P9; RWB-E1-013 §7 and §11
section: RWB-E1-013 §7 Acceptance criteria and §11 Data; this story §7, §11 and §16
description: The legacy story asserts measure values (120 cases of which 60 Mortgage, realized recovery of 4,350,000.00 THB), a definition version in force and a frozen snapshot, and its section 11 writes nine measure_definition and twelve measure_snapshot fields. All of those belong to rwb_reporting under the ownership map, so the P1 slice produces no measure value and reads no measure table, and the legacy figures of AC2 and AC6 are asserted by P9 and by the integration suite. No source states which measure figures, if any, this service supplies.
evidence: Ownership map owner P9 for measure_definition and measure_snapshot; Arch v5 slide 15 P9 OUT (measures, snapshots) and P1 OUT (freshness, reconciliation); TSD P1 T3.6 has no measure table
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-013 AC1, AC2, AC5, AC8 and §11
proposed: Read this slice as supplying the facts and the gate only: listEligibleAccounts, snapshot(page), the payments since entry, the freshness stamp and the reconciliation. Assert no measure code, definition version, baseline date value or total in this story, and leave every measure figure with RWB-P9-E1013-APP and RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG.

title: The readiness and status operation shapes are fixed only in part by the architecture text
source: Architecture v5 slide 32 (POST /v1/business-days/{date}/ready answered 202 and idempotent; GET /v1/business-days/{date}/status answers RUNNING, DONE or LATE); API Specification v4 and TSD P1 appendix T-A name neither path
section: This story §12.1 and §9
description: The architecture gives the two paths, the 202 answer, the idempotency on the business date and the three status values, but no source fixes the request and response schema of either operation, the cursor or page shape of snapshot(page), or the field names of the freshness and payments answers. The API Specification v4 and the TSD P1 appendix list the freshness and data-product paths but not the readiness, status or payments paths, so those three are named by the architecture catalogue only.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 32 interface contract line; slide 15 and the service catalogue note for rwb-source-data; TSD P1 T-A.1 endpoint inventory (API-P1-001 to API-P1-016, no readiness, status or payments path); integration story RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG section 12.2 calling the same three paths
owner_role: Solution architect and TechX contract owner
proposed: Fix the four paths, the 202 and the three status values in the P1 OpenAPI document of the epic's contract story, use the path names already called by RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG, and let the field names follow the field IDs of the P1 logical data model.

title: The gate answers COMPLETE or HOLD while the freshness list of values holds LOADED and STALE
source: TSD P1 v3 T3.7 and T3.8 (LOV-FRESHNESS: LOADED, STALE); integration story RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG section 9 (daily gate COMPLETE or HOLD)
section: This story §9 and §12.1
description: The freshness stamp of a data product carries LOADED or STALE from LOV-FRESHNESS, and the daily gate of the same date answers COMPLETE or HOLD as the integration slice states it. Two vocabularies describe the same condition, no list of values holds the gate pair, and the naming of the gate value in the readiness status answer is fixed by no source.
evidence: TSD P1 T3.7 (status LOADED or STALE) and T3.8 LOV-FRESHNESS; Architecture v5 slide 32 (status RUNNING, DONE, LATE); integration story section 9 gate rows
proposed: Keep both as they are read: the stamp carries LOADED or STALE per product and the gate carries COMPLETE or HOLD for the date, and add the gate pair to the list of values in the next P1 TSD version so one vocabulary per level is documented.

title: MSG-P1-001 now names the ACE batch where the legacy story and the integration copy name a load
source: FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 VR-P1-001-1 and open point OQ-P1-07; TSD P1 v3 T3.7; RWB-E1-013 §14; integration story RWB-ITG-E1013-ITG section 14
section: RWB-E1-013 §14 Validation and messages; this story §14
description: The FSD P1 and TSD P1 wording of MSG-P1-001 is "{product} is from {date}. Today's ACE batch has not arrived." and the FSD open point OQ-P1-07 records that the message now names the ACE batch rather than a load or ALS and that the message standard still needs the same change. The legacy story and the integration copy of it read "{product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived." The ID and the two placeholders are the same in both; the second sentence differs.
evidence: FSD P1 VR-P1-001-1 and OQ-P1-07; TSD P1 T3.7; RWB-E1-013 section 14; integration story section 14 (five texts copied unchanged from the legacy story)
proposed: Use the FSD P1 and TSD P1 wording in this service, which is the higher source under R-PREC, and update the message standard and the legacy copy to the same sentence so one text is in force.

title: rwb-source-data view slice: how legacy RWB-E1-069 splits across three stories, where the two view migrations sit on the per-service sequence, and the response shape of the read operations are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 8, 11, 12 and 13; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A2.1; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T2, T3.2, T3.3 and T6.3; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 11, 13, 15, 29, 41 and 45; Template and Rules v1 DP-05, DP-11 and DP-15
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 1 to 7; section 7 AC1 to AC8 and the Target reading; section 11; section 12.1; section 12.7; section 13 Migrations and sequence
description: Four things this slice needs are absent. (1) The legacy story puts the four extension tables, the 16 Section A views, the 14 Section B views and the grant block in two migrations of one schema, and no source states how that set splits across an application story, a database story and an integration story, which of them owns the grant statements, or where the 30 views live once the schema is split 19 ways. (2) The legacy story places the three helper functions twice: its preconditions say V0001 created them, its flow step 1 and TSD P1 T3.2 put them in the Section A migration. (3) The two legacy migration numbers belong to one monolith sequence, and no source states their position on the per-service sequence. (4) The response field names and the problem body of the three read operations are named by no source.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 3 reads 'RWB-E1-001 is done: V0001 created the recovery tables, the three helper functions recovery.ace_to_date, recovery.ace_to_boolean and recovery.ace_mask_value, the dictionary rows and the view v_data_dictionary' while its flow step 1 reads 'takes Section A of ... into V0002__rwb_e1_069_ace_source_views.sql: the 16 views, the three helper functions and the grant block'; its section 12 reads 'No endpoint and no event. The contract is the migration set and the grant'; TSD P1 T3.2 lists the helper functions inside the Section A migration and names the two migrations 'proposed V0002, next free sequence at merge'; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 29 give the read path as a SQL view on the rwb_source_data login and name no response field; no extract states which story of the split owns which statement.
area: rwb-source-data view slice and migration split
proposed: Publish the three read operations with their response fields and problem body in RWB-P1-E1069-CON, and record in the Service Contract Catalog that the view SQL, the helper functions and the conformance test are rwb-source-data's application slice, the login, the grants, the view owner and the four extension tables its database slice, and the 19-login proof the wave 1 integration slice.

title: The ACE read is a REST contract of rwb-source-data in Architecture v5 and an in-process Java interface in TSD P1 and legacy RWB-E1-069
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 13, 15, 41 and 45; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T2 (AceSourceReadRepository) and T5.2; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.1; Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12; Template and Rules v1 R3 (source precedence) and DP-05, DP-11
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 4 Flow step 8 and 9; section 12.1; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The two sources disagree on the shape of the cross-service read. Architecture v5 makes it a REST contract of rwb-source-data on its own base, with a one-hop budget and a 2 s timeout, and states that only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views while every other service asks it over REST or a Temporal activity. TSD P1 v3 T2 and T5.2 make it the published Java interface AceSourceReadRepository ('Other modules read ACE data through P1's AceSourceReadRepository interface, and through no other path'), and legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 states 'No endpoint and no event'. The precedence list of Template and Rules R3 puts the Architecture catalogue slides first, so the REST contract wins and the TSD wording is recorded for the next TSD version.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 15 reads 'REST GET /customers/{id}, /accounts/{id} · GET /collateral/{id}, /payments?accountId= · GET /freshness (business date) · POST /business-days/{date}/ready (Airflow)' and 'SQL ACE DB views: SELECT recovery.v_ace_* (30 views)'; slide 41 gives the first API path of rwb-source-data as '/customers/{id}'; slide 45 reads 'Only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views (ADR-010). Everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity'; TSD P1 T2 reads 'Published interface | Java interface other modules call: freshness, the ACE read methods and the dictionary. No table is read across modules' and T5.2 reads 'Other modules read ACE data through P1's AceSourceReadRepository interface, and through no other path'; legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 reads 'No endpoint and no event. The contract is the migration set and the grant'.
proposed: Adopt the REST contract of Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41 on base /api/recovery/source-data/v1 with a 2 s client budget, keep AceSourceReadRepository as the owning service's internal repository, and carry the TSD P1 T2 and T5.2 wording to the next TSD version as a change note.

title: rwb-source-data database slice: who creates the login and holds its credential, the exact grant names, the position of the three grant migrations on the sequence, and the platform sequence dependency of a Day-1 database story are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 4 steps 1 to 7, 10, 12 and 13; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T6.3; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.4; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11, 29 and 41; Template and Rules v1 DP-02, DP-15 and R5.7
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 5; section 7 AC1 to AC8; section 12.7; section 13 Sequencing and Schema privileges and revokes
description: Four values this slice needs are absent. (1) The legacy story names the service role recovery_svc and assumes it exists, with no statement of who creates the login, who holds its credential or how the credential is rotated. (2) No source gives the name of a single grant privilege set: the legacy block grants one view at a time and revokes PUBLIC on all tables of schema recovery, while Arch v5 states each login owns its own schema, so whether the login also needs an explicit USAGE grant on its own schema is unstated. (3) The three migrations of this slice interleave with the two view migrations of the application slice, and no source fixes their order or their version numbers on the per-service sequence. (4) The Work Package fixes 'Depends on (build)' as None for this Day-1 database story, while the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15 carries the platform contract RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, so that dependency has no metadata row to sit in.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 3 reads 'The roles ace_view_owner and recovery_svc exist in DEV and SIT, with the names fixed in the Environment and Deployment Design' and its section 12 reads 'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO recovery_svc' with no statement of ownership or credential; TSD P1 T6.3 reads 'Recovery service identity | USAGE on schema recovery; SELECT on the views. No SELECT on any public table'; Architecture v5 slide 29 reads 'one login per service; grants on its own schema' and names 'login rwb_source_data', slide 11 reads 'Identity | ... | One login: rwb_source_data'; TSD P1 T3.2 names the two view migrations 'proposed V0002, next free sequence at merge' and fixes no order against a grant migration; the Work Package lists 'H': [] and 'Ready to start': 'Day 1' for RWB-P1-E1069-DB.
area: rwb-source-data login, grants and migration order
proposed: Publish in the Service Template Specification the login creation and credential policy, the exact grant and revoke list with the order of the three migrations on the sequence, and record RWB-PLT-E1044-CON as the platform dependency of every per-service database story so a Day-1 story carries it without breaking the Day-1 rule.

title: The service role is recovery_svc on one recovery schema in TSD P1 and legacy RWB-E1-069, and a per-service login rwb_source_data with its own schema under Architecture v5
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 11, 29, 37 and 41; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T1.1, T6.3; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.2 and A1.3; Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 3, 11 and 12; Template and Rules v1 R3 and DP-02
section: Section 1 Story; section 2 Business rationale; section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC1 to AC4; section 13 Grant block and Schema privileges and revokes
description: The sources disagree on the identity model. Architecture v5 splits the one recovery schema into 19 rwb_* schemas with one login each, states that each login owns its own schema and has no grant on any other schema, and gives the login of this service as rwb_source_data with SELECT only on the views. TSD P1 v3 T6.3 and FSD P1 v3 A1.2 still describe a single recovery schema with the recovery service identity holding USAGE on schema recovery and SELECT on the views, and legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 grants USAGE on schema recovery to recovery_svc. The precedence list puts Architecture v5 first, so the login is renamed and its own schema added, and the USAGE grant on schema recovery stays because the 30 views stay in that schema.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 29 reads 'rwb-source-data / login rwb_source_data / recovery.v_ace_* views: SELECT only' and 'each service has one database login that owns its schema and has no grant on any other schema; only rwb_source_data has SELECT on the views'; slide 37 reads '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' against 'Views read only by rwb-source-data'; TSD P1 T6.3 reads 'Recovery service identity | USAGE on schema recovery; SELECT on the views' with no per-service schema; FSD P1 A1.2 reads 'The recovery service identity holds SELECT on the views and nothing else'; legacy RWB-E1-069 section 12 reads 'GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA recovery TO recovery_svc'.
proposed: Rename the service role to rwb_source_data in the next versions of TSD P1 and FSD P1, state the per-service schema and the USAGE grant on schema recovery in one row of the Service Template Specification, and record the rename in the Change Register against DP-02.

title: The number of Tier 1 ACE tables is 21 in legacy RWB-E1-069 and 22 in FSD P1 and TSD P1, and the grant list is enumerated only in the legacy story
source: Legacy RWB-E1-069 sections 11 and 12; FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 A1.3; TSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 T6.3
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 7 AC4; section 13 Grant block
description: The legacy story says Section A reads 21 ACE tables and prints the 21 table names in its section 12 grant block, while FSD P1 A1.3 and TSD P1 T6.3 say the view owner holds SELECT on 'the 22 Tier 1 ACE tables'. The two FSD and TSD rows are the higher sources on a technical count, but neither enumerates a 22nd table, and the grant block of the legacy story is the only enumeration in any source. This story keeps the 21 named tables, so the grant it writes is exactly the list the legacy story gives, and the count conflict is raised for the ACE team to confirm before the grant is released.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-069 section 11 reads 'Section A reads 21 ACE tables: account, payment, customer, phone, email, address, ca_relation, aa_relation, collateral, asset, efs_action, efs_action_code, efs_assignment, bucket_log_snapshot, product, branch, bot_holiday, ace_case, cfsc_mg_ssme_tdr_case, tdr_calculation and ai_recommended_plan' and its section 12 grants SELECT on exactly those names; FSD P1 A1.3 reads '1. 22 ACE tables that exist today | ACE team, read only | Reads through 16 Section A views'; TSD P1 T6.3 reads 'ace_view_owner | Dedicated NOLOGIN role. Holds SELECT on the 22 Tier 1 ACE tables, and on the Tier 2 tables once RWB-ACE-001 lands'.
area: ACE Tier 1 table list and the view owner grant
proposed: Have the ACE team lead confirm the Tier 1 table list, publish the 21 names or the name of the 22nd table in the next versions of FSD P1 and TSD P1, and keep the legacy grant block as the enumeration until then.
